declarations.docstring: Finite representation type for an adjacency matrix: it admits a simple orientation, and every such orientation over every algebraically closed field has a finite set of indecomposable representatives exhausting all finite-dimensional indecomposables up to isomorphism.
A zero-one matrix admitting the orientation bundled into the finite-type predicate has zero diagonal. This uses the orientation's prohibition of self-arrows, not representation finiteness.
Isomorphism of quiver representations: vertexwise linear equivalences commuting with all arrows.
